_meta.indication: AMONDYS 45 is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 45 skipping; approved under accelerated approval based on an increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial with a 96-week randomized double-blind period followed by a 48-week open-label period; casimersen arm randomized 2:1 casimersen (30 mg/kg/week IV) vs placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Male patients aged 7 to 13 years with an established clinical diagnosis of DMD amenable to exon 45 skipping, on a stable dose of corticosteroids.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: For accelerated approval: change from Baseline to Week 48 in dystrophin protein expression in biopsied muscle, as measured by western blot (a surrogate endpoint). The trial's primary clinical endpoint is change from baseline in the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at Week 96.
pivotal_trials.n: Interim biomarker analysis set: 43 evaluable patients (27 casimersen, 16 placebo). Overall casimersen-arm safety population: 57 casimersen and 31 placebo.
pivotal_trials.result: Truncated dystrophin by western blot increased from 0.9% of normal at Baseline to 1.7% at Week 48 in casimersen vs 0.5% to 0.8% in placebo; mean difference 0.59%, p = 0.004. Exon 45 skipping increased with a mean difference of 1.599; p < 0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >20% and at least 5% higher than placebo): upper respiratory tract infection (65% vs 55%), cough (33% vs 26%), pyrexia (33% vs 23%), headache (32% vs 19%), arthralgia (21% vs 10%), and oropharyngeal pain (21% vs 7%). Warnings: hypersensitivity reactions (including angioedema and anaphylaxis) and potential kidney toxicity based on animal data.
target_moa: Casimersen is an antisense oligonucleotide (phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer, PMO) designed to bind exon 45 of dystrophin pre-mRNA, causing exclusion of this exon during mRNA processing to restore the reading frame and produce an internally truncated but functional dystrophin protein.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was planned or convened for this application.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle (dystrophin protein expression measured by western blot), proposed as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This application provides dystrophin biomarker data proposed as a surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in support of the accelerated approval of casimersen for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients with a confirmed DMD mutation amenable to exon 45 skipping.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Complete Study 4045-301 (ESSENCE), the ongoing randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled confirmatory trial with the 6-minute walk test as primary endpoint, to verify clinical benefit.

summary.text: Casimersen received accelerated approval based on a dystrophin biomarker surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with Study 4045-301 (ESSENCE) required as the confirmatory trial. The application also had Fast Track designation (7/24/14), Orphan Drug designation (9/4/19), and Priority Review (granted 8/24/20).
